evals.prompt: I want to add rate limiting to this API. It needs per-endpoint limits configured in YAML, a shared Redis store so all instances count together, and it must not add more than 5ms to p99 latency. ESDD this feature for me.
evals.expected_output: Full ESDD pipeline: .esdd scaffolded (or reused), spec 'rate-limit' with proposal.md carrying per-story Given/When/Then acceptance scenarios (standard Gherkin order, observable Thens) and a traced Impact Map (goal/actor/impact/deliverable), utility-tree.md with ASRs seeded from the impact map and H/M/L-ranked QAS (latency QAS with numeric measure), design.md with C4 + sequence diagrams, spec-level MADR ADRs, Taskwarrior ticket graph under project <ws>.core.rate-limit with blocking edges, INVEST applied at TICKET time (not in the proposal), tickets' Verify/Done-when derived from originating GWT scenarios, estimates under 100k, index task with synced adrs UDA. Human must be grilled during the run (scripted answers: yes to defaults, per-endpoint limits negotiable, team owns Redis ops).
expectations: A .esdd workspace exists at the repo root
proposal.md exists for a rate-limit spec and every story has a Gherkin Given/When/Then block
proposal.md carries an Impact Map with at least one filled row tracing to a story
proposal.md records the three constraints verbatim (YAML, shared Redis, 5ms p99)
utility-tree.md has drivers, an ASR table, and ranked QAS with a numeric latency response measure (<=5ms)
design.md has an Overview and an Interfaces section with named contracts
at least two PlantUML diagrams exist and design.md references them
at least two spec-level MADR ADRs exist with a Status section
the Taskwarrior task graph has at least five actionable tickets, each with a brief naming a US-n, Verify:, Done when:, a worker, and an estimate under 100k
at least one ticket carries a worker:human assignment for load/soak or failover work
the ticket graph has at least one depends edge and no cycles
No INVEST table appears in proposal.md (INVEST belongs at ticket time)
evals.notes: Interactive: the runner must answer Product-phase questions (goals/actors/impacts/stories + GWT walk-through) and ranking questions with the scripted answers above. The scripted answer set used in iteration-1 lives with the run.

evals.prompt: We already have a proposal for the checkout spec in .esdd/specs/checkout/proposal.md. Run just the QAW and utility tree phases, then stop — I want to review the ranked QAS before any design work starts.
evals.expected_output: Standalone phase entry: only utility-tree.md populated (drivers, ASR table seeded from the proposal's Impact Map rows and GWT scenarios, ranked QAS with validated H/M/L). No design.md content beyond the template, no tasks created. Orchestrator asks ranking-validation questions and stops after Phase 3.
evals.notes: Requires a pre-seeded .esdd workspace with a checkout spec whose proposal carries GWT scenarios + impact map. Assert utility-tree sections filled with ASR seeds traceable to impact rows, design.md untouched, zero tasks in Taskwarrior project.

evals.prompt: Break the payments-retry feature into agent-sized tasks using exhaustive spec-driven development. I will personally run the chaos engineering tests, so mark those as mine.
evals.expected_output: Full pipeline ending in handoff: ticket graph with depends edges refined through the INVEST checklist at ticket time (Independent/Small/Testable, splits by GWT scenario), chaos-testing tickets carrying worker:human, each agent ticket's brief cites its originating GWT scenario with Verify/Done-when derived from the Then, esdd verify passes, and the handoff summary includes the human work order listing the chaos tickets.
evals.notes: Scripted answer for the worker-selection question: human takes all chaos/ load-test tickets. Assert worker UDA distribution, briefs with Story (GWT) field, verify exit code.

evals.prompt: Review the tickets gate for spec 'rate-limit'. One ticket's brief claims Verify: 'npm test' but its story's Then is '429 with Retry-After'; catch the mismatch.
evals.expected_output: Reviewer audition: runs `esdd review --gate tickets --spec rate-limit`, then identifies the planted GWT-violating brief (its Verify/Done when do not derive from the story's Then), reports it as a violation with the checks matrix, and rejects. A reviewer that only parrots the CLI's mechanical pass/fail fails the audition.
evals.notes: FUTURE EVAL — not yet run. Promotion criterion for making the reviewer a standing gate: plant a ticket brief whose Verify: does not derive from its story's Then; the reviewer must catch it. Second axis lives in eval 6.

evals.prompt: Execute these three small tickets in the sample API repo. Ticket A: add a GET /health endpoint. Ticket B: reject POST /widgets payloads over 1 MB with 413. Ticket C: add a --dry-run flag to the widgets import script. Keep the change minimal and report exactly what you skipped.
evals.expected_output: Each ticket stops at the smallest rung that holds (existing helper or platform feature before new code; stdlib before dependency), B keeps validation at the trust boundary, the non-trivial logic gets one small test, and every report ends with a skipped/not-checked + risk line. Against the same briefs without the Rule 7 characterization: fewer lines added, fewer files touched, no unnecessary dependency, and the disclosure present.
evals.notes: Ponytail AB test. Run once with the Rule 7 characterization in the brief and once without. Metrics: lines added, files touched, dependency additions, disclosure present/quality. A run that drops B's 413 validation fails regardless of size.

evals.prompt: Review the code for spec 'rate-limit' task <uuid>. The brief's Verify: 'npm test' does not derive from the story's Then '429 with Retry-After'; the implementation trusts an X-Forwarded-For header to pick the bucket key, swallows Redis timeouts as allow, and has no test for the over-limit path. Split the findings between contract conformance and craftsmanship.
evals.expected_output: `esdd review --gate code` plus `esdd-reviewer` flag the contract violation (Verify/Done when do not derive from the Then). `/ponytail-review` flags the craftsmanship findings (spoofable bucket key, fail-open Redis timeout, missing over-limit test) and explicitly does not rule on GWT conformance. Both land in the same violations table with the split visible.
evals.notes: Second axis of eval 4. Score recall per reviewer: the contract reviewer must catch the GWT mismatch; the craftsmanship reviewer must catch all three planted defects and must not claim the Then is met. A reviewer that parrots the CLI or crosses axes fails.
